title: Fraud Detection & Transaction Analysis
short_description: Learn how financial systems analyze transaction streams, detect suspicious patterns, identify unusual activity, and efficiently process transaction values.

real_world_context.problem: A financial system analyzes streams of transactions to identify unusual patterns, repeated activity, suspicious combinations, threshold-crossing values, and transaction codes that differ from expected behavior.
real_world_context.why_it_matters: Efficient transaction analysis allows financial monitoring systems to process large volumes of transactions and quickly identify patterns or values that may require further investigation.

learning_objectives: Apply KMP Pattern Matching to locate suspicious transaction patterns efficiently.
Use Sliding Window techniques to analyze transaction activity over fixed-size windows.
Apply Binary Search to quickly locate the first transaction crossing a suspicious threshold.
Use Sorting and Two Pointer techniques to identify suspicious transaction combinations.
Understand how the Single Number technique can identify an unmatched transaction code.
Apply Bit Manipulation to count the set bits of a unique transaction code.
Understand how different algorithms can be combined to analyze large transaction datasets efficiently.
Choose an appropriate algorithm based on the type of transaction-analysis requirement.

real_world_mapping.transaction_stream: Sequence of transaction codes or transaction records
real_world_mapping.transaction_amount: Numerical value associated with a transaction
real_world_mapping.transaction_pattern: Sequence of transaction codes representing a suspicious activity pattern
real_world_mapping.monitoring_window: Fixed-size consecutive group of transactions analyzed together
real_world_mapping.suspicious_threshold: Transaction amount at or above which additional analysis may be required
real_world_mapping.suspicious_combination: Pair of transaction amounts satisfying a predefined target condition
real_world_mapping.transaction_code: Numeric identifier associated with a transaction record
real_world_mapping.unique_transaction_code: Transaction code that occurs once while other codes occur in pairs
real_world_mapping.set_bits: Number of active binary bits in a transaction code
real_world_mapping.fraud_detection: Process of identifying unusual or potentially suspicious transaction behavior

completion_message: You have completed the Fraud Detection & Transaction Analysis mission. You have learned how pattern matching, sliding windows, binary search, sorting, two pointer techniques, and bit manipulation can be applied to transaction monitoring and fraud-analysis problems.
